toast.paired_later: Paired – will sync when the server is reachable

err.invalid_url: Please enter a valid http(s) URL.
err.timeout: The Collector did not answer in time.
err.unreachable: Server not reachable – check the server address in Settings.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.count_one: {n} new – decide: read now, later or not interested.
inbox.count_other: {n} new – decide: read now, later or not interested.
inbox.clear_hint: Mark all shown entries as not interested
inbox.empty_text: Follow any website – with or without RSS – and the Collector turns it into entries.

reading.title: Read now
reading.text: What you are reading right now. Mark it done when you are through.
reading.hint: Pick something from your inbox or your later list.

later.title: Later
later.text: Your reading list – synced across your devices.
later.hint: Save entries from the inbox with “Later”.

done.title: Done
done.text: Finished reading. The most recent 300 are shown.

feeds.title: Feeds
feeds.follow_text: A feed URL or any page – the Collector finds the entries (direct, discovered, guessed, sitemap or HTML).
feeds.shared: Shared link received – press Follow to subscribe.
feeds.unfollow_body: {title} disappears from all your devices. Entries you saved for later stay in your list.
feeds.io_text: Coming from Feedly or another reader? Import its OPML export. Adding via the share sheet works once News is installed; on desktop drag this bookmarklet to your bookmarks bar:
feeds.import_invalid: This is not a valid OPML file.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: News {version} · your data stays on your devices – the server only sees encrypted blobs.
settings.swipe_text: Choose what a swipe on an entry does. Applies on touch screens; saved on this device.
settings.server_text: News fetches all feeds through the Collector on this server and syncs through it. Default: the server News is served from – or your own instance.
settings.test_wrong: Server answered, but this is not a News Reader server.
settings.test_fail: Not reachable. Check the address, HTTPS certificate and your connection.
settings.sync_paired: This device is paired. Scan the code with your phone (or open the link on another device) to share feeds, reading list and states. No account – whoever has the link has access, so keep it private.
settings.sync_intro: News works fully offline on this device. To sync with your phone or another browser, create a sync vault. Everything is encrypted on this device before it leaves – the server stores one unreadable blob. No account, no e-mail, no database.
settings.sync_https: Sync needs HTTPS (or localhost) – this page is served insecurely.
settings.join_title: Already set up on another device?
settings.join_text: Scan its QR code, or paste its pairing link or key here.
settings.join_invalid: That is neither a pairing link nor a vault key.
settings.local_text: {feeds} feed records, {items} item states, {entries} cached entries on this device.

dlg.clear_done_body_one: {n} finished entry will be removed. It won’t reappear in the inbox.
dlg.clear_done_body_other: {n} finished entries will be removed. They won’t reappear in the inbox.
dlg.unpair_body: This device stops syncing. Your local data stays here, and other devices keep the vault.
dlg.wipe_body:
The encrypted vault is removed from the server. Devices keep their local data; the next sync of any paired device uploads it again.

Use “Unpair” on every device first if you want the vault gone for good.
dlg.reset_body: Deletes all feeds, states and cached entries from this browser. Synced data on the server is not touched – pair again to restore it.
dlg.pair_body: This device will share feeds, reading list and states with every device that uses this vault.
dlg.pair_merge: Existing data on this device is merged – nothing is lost.

sync.local_long: Not paired – data stays on this device
sync.https: Sync needs HTTPS (or localhost) for encryption.
sync.conflict: Too many concurrent changes – will retry.
sync.decrypt: Vault could not be decrypted – wrong key or damaged data.
sync.format: Unknown vault format on the server.

reader.unavailable: You are offline – this article was not saved for offline reading.
reader.partial: Only part of this article could be saved – the page is behind a paywall or built with JavaScript.
